title: Reference train prerequisites as train:{train_id}

facts.note: Train specification files are identifiable by kind; the dependencies section lives in the train spec. Fires on authoring, editing, reviewing or validating any train spec, not only on dependency edits.
Planning task text mentions trains, their ordering or prerequisites.

values: train dependency list added or edited
facts.note: Needs a diff-level observer that detects train spec changes, including the dependencies field.

values: consumer train missing dependency on its producer train
facts.note: Needs a detector that validates every existing dependency entry's format and walks the whole train dependency graph (including self-edges) for cycles; the producer/consumer check is llm_judged unless train-level produce/consume data is available.

fires: Planner authors a new train that needs another train's outputs or foundation first
Planner edits the dependencies list of an existing train
Planner adds or edits a train that consumes data produced by another train
Planner reviews or validates existing train specs, including ones whose dependencies list contains malformed references, a self-reference, or a cycle
Planner edits any part of a train spec whose existing dependencies violate the reference format or form a cycle
doesNotFire: Editing a wagon's internal acceptances or WMBTs without touching or reviewing any train spec
Authoring documentation or plans that do not define, edit or validate train specs

given: A train spec exists or is being authored, edited, reviewed or validated, with or without existing dependency entries
when: The planner writes, changes or checks that train's dependencies
then: Every entry in the train's dependencies must be a prerequisite train reference of the form train:{train_id} matching ^train:[0-9]{2}-[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$.
prefer: Foundation (commons) trains, such as authentication/session foundations, often precede the trains that build on them (foundation_first); order them first when that applies — this is a frequent pattern, not an unconditional requirement.
avoid: A data-flow consumer train that does not depend on the train producing the data it consumes — consumers must depend on producers (data_flow).
Circular dependencies between trains — direct, transitive, or a train listing itself — are forbidden.
Free-text, bare-id or wagon references in the dependencies list instead of train:{train_id}.
Reversing direction: making a producer depend on its consumer.
why: A dependency is a prerequisite train reference; a uniform train:{train_id} form lets tooling resolve ordering, consumers need their producers first, and a cycle makes the trains impossible to sequence.
evidence: Every entry in each train's dependencies matches ^train:[0-9]{2}-[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$ and resolves to an existing train.
A graph walk over all train dependencies (including self-edges) finds no cycle.
Each consumer train lists the train producing its consumed data among its dependencies; no producer depends on its consumer.
verifier_detail: Term 'dependency' = a prerequisite train reference; pattern ^train:[0-9]{2}-[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$; circular: forbidden.
Source example (data_flow): train:30-match-solo depends on train:21-scenario-curation.
Validate existing entries on every train spec, not only changed ones; a train referencing itself is a cycle of length one.

splitSuggestion.then: The train dependency graph must contain no direct, transitive or self-referential cycle.
A train that consumes data produced by another train must list that producer train among its dependencies.

additions.text: The source statement holds three independent obligations: reference format (kept in then), acyclicity (planner.train.dependencies-acyclic) and consumer-depends-on-producer (planner.train.dependencies-data-flow). The latter two are stated normatively in avoid here until split.
Free-text, bare-id or wagon references; producer depending on its consumer; a train listing itself treated as a cycle.
additions.justification: Concrete anti-patterns derived directly from the required pattern, the data_flow direction and 'circular: forbidden' (a self-reference is the shortest cycle); no new obligation.

additions.text: References resolve to an existing train.
additions.justification: A prerequisite reference is only meaningful if it names a real train (graph edge runs_alongside planner.train.registry).

additions.text: Validate existing entries on every train spec, not only changed ones.
additions.justification: The source prohibitions apply to train dependencies generally, not only to edits (auditor activation finding).
